evals.prompt: Here's the brief and Design Spec for showing a seller's floor price on the company page and the sell indication page: https://app.notion.com/p/EXAMPLE-offer-floors-brief. What screens does this touch and how should we design it?
evals.expected_output: Places the work with design-os-system-map (readout only, no FigJam), finds each current screen starting from the Design Spec's Where this lives links, classifies both screens as Compose, recommends Coded hi-fi with reasons and confidence, shows the readout table, and asks for one yes. On yes, rebuilds both screens as they ship, commits that baseline before any change, adds a Today/Proposed Design choice, and hands off to design-os-prototype From a brief.
expectations: Checks design-os-system-map is installed before running it, and asks for no FigJam
Uses the Design Spec's Where this lives links as the first screen source
Each affected screen row has page, owner, change, path, and current reference with source and confidence
Classifies both screens as Compose, in those words
Recommends exactly one route, Coded hi-fi, with reasons tied to screens and a confidence
Builds nothing before the person says yes
After yes, the as-is baseline is committed before any brief change is applied
Playground has a Design choice with Today and Proposed values
Hands off to design-os-prototype From a brief

evals.prompt: TRA-123: let sellers get offer alerts on WhatsApp and add a new 'alert rules' section to account settings. Does this need a designer?
evals.expected_output: Fetches the Linear issue and its brief, places it, finds the current account settings screen, classifies the WhatsApp channel and the new section as Extend, recommends Designer, and after a yes writes the handoff package for the owning team's Design lead, looked up fresh in the Product Team Directory. Offers it as a Linear comment or a Notion page on the initiative record and writes only after a yes. No Slack draft.
expectations: Classifies the WhatsApp alerts and the new settings section as Extend
Recommends the Designer route because of Extend and the non-web channel
Looks up the Design lead through pm-os-clarity-context People lookup and the Product Team Directory, not from memory
Handoff package has the brief link, why it needs a designer, affected screens, Extend candidates and Alloy gaps, open questions, placement, and a suggested next skill
Offers a Linear comment or a Notion page and writes neither without a yes
Does not draft a Slack message
No person's name appears in anything saved for reuse; the name appears only in the package itself

evals.prompt: I'm a PM with only a brief so far (no Design Spec) for a new multi-step buyer onboarding checklist. I need something clickable for the M scope review next week to check the steps make sense.
evals.expected_output: Reads the brief, notes there's no Design Spec, places it, finds the current onboarding screens (or says none were found), and recommends Coded wires because it's a flow question in a brief-only scope review. On yes, rebuilds the current onboarding screens as they ship, commits the baseline, then hands to design-os-prototype From a brief at wires fidelity.
expectations: States that no Design Spec exists
Records a source and confidence for each current onboarding screen, or says none found and what was checked
Recommends Coded wires, citing the brief-only scope review and the flow question
Hands off to design-os-prototype From a brief with wires fidelity
Commits the as-is baseline before applying the brief

evals.prompt: Our team wants to add a 'Clarity fund available' banner on the company page, which another team owns, plus a small edit to our own fund details page. Just tell me how to design it and start.
evals.expected_output: Places it, sees the company page is owned by another team, finds that team's current frame in its Figma files (preferring ready-for-dev pages), marks the banner change as needing that team's sign-off, and recommends Figma (or Designer if the change is contested or a new pattern), never a lighter route. On yes to Figma, asks the person to duplicate the owning team's file, never edits the original, clones the affected frames onto a '<feature> · design impact' page in the copy, and annotates the changes.
expectations: Marks the company page change as cross-team with 'needs <team> sign-off'
Recommends Figma or Designer, not Coded hi-fi or wires
Prefers a shipped or ready-for-dev frame over explorations, and says which it used
Never edits the owning team's Figma file; asks the person to duplicate it first
In the copy, creates a page named '<feature> · design impact' with the affected frames cloned and annotated
Confirms before the Figma write
Ends the readout with a 'Map suggestion: link <page> card to <frame>' line

evals.prompt: The 'Download transaction history' button on the company page is returning a 500. What's the design impact?
evals.expected_output: Places it on the company page, finds the current screen, classifies it as Fix (no visible change), recommends No design, and offers pm-os-ticket-brief rather than starting any build.
expectations: Classifies the screen as Fix
Recommends the No design route
Offers pm-os-ticket-brief as the next step
Starts no prototype or Figma work
